title: Companion Virtual Home plates, v1
description: The contract between Companion Virtual Home (which renders a 3D house into overlay-free per-beat plates) and the video-kit (which composes them into landscape and portrait films with `ci-video import-home`). A JSON file, not an import: neither side loads the other's code. The normative text is PLATES.md; where this schema and `src/sources/virtual-home.ts` disagree, the code is what the kit enforces and this is a bug in the schema. Every path is relative to the folder plates.json is in and may not leave it. Every string a viewer reads is checked for em and en dashes, exclamation marks, banned words and the word "beta".

v.description: The contract version. A kit reads the version it was written for and refuses any other.

kind.description: family-film: a fictional family's story told beat by beat (family is required). home-tour: a home with no family (family must be null).

id.description: A family slug or a home's display id. Never a builder handle or a house id. It becomes the film's name: out/<id>-landscape.mp4.

displayName.description: The title card: 'The Fenwick family of Marlowe'. A home's display name, never the name its spec was filed under.

tagline.description: The line under the title on the poster card.

lighting.description: Day only. The owner's ruling of 2026-10-22: films are lit as day, never dusk or night.

fps.description: Frames a second of every plate. Virtual Home renders 30.

profile.description: Provenance of the render (browser build, GPU path, ffmpeg). Recorded, never interpreted.

text.description: The strings the kit prints, resolved by the renderer from its claims file so the kit never parses claims.

label.description: Shown on every frame in a corner pill: 'Fictional family. Real software.' May not be empty.

cta.description: The last line of the film. The fleet closes on 'UnCloud your life.'

tagline.description: The line under the call to action: 'See Companion Core'.

link.description: The only link an end card of a home film carries.

codaTitle.description: The heading of the disclosure card. Default 'Said plainly'.

disclosures.description: The disclosures the end card prints, verbatim, in order.

hook.description: The claim the 15 s and 30 s cuts open on (the owner-approved line, resolved from the claims file). Without it only the film is written.

accent.description: A phrase, or phrases, of the text to set in the accent colour. Each must appear in the text as whole words.

beats.description: One entry per beat, in film order. The first is usually an approach plate with no member.

inserts.description: Real, whole, unedited screenshots that may be shown as labelled full-frame inserts between the apps and the end card. Never composited into a plate.

cuts.description: The beats each short cut shows, by cut length in seconds. Absent, the kit picks the first moments of the film, one per person.

audio.description: null for a silent, captioned film (the state until the local model is approved). Otherwise the local Kokoro recordings, one per beat that is read.

platesSha.description: Digest of all the plates, for the renderer's cache.

claimsSha.description: Digest of the claims file the text was resolved from.

inputsSha.description: Digest of everything the render was a function of.

rect.description: A rectangle as fractions of the frame, inside it.

id.description: Kebab-case; a scene id and a filename. title, hook, apps, apps-N, proof-N, close, plainly and label are the kit's own and are refused.

companion.description: The companion's name. Recorded, not printed.

member.description: Whose beat it is. Their name is the chapter kicker. null for an approach plate.

title.description: The caption, in the lower third. Two lines at most.

body.description: The beat's words. Shown as one cue across the beat when `cues` is absent and the beat is not read aloud.

chips.description: The apps in this beat, in order of appearance. The apps scene lists each app once.

app.description: The app's name. A logo is only ever shown beside it.

logo.description: A .png, .webp or .jpg beside plates.json. The real logo, identified by the name next to it.

pairText.description: '<app>, alternative to <service>', exactly as the renderer's pair rules write it. Never 'replaces'.

cues.description: Caption cues from the renderer's clock, seconds from the start of the plate. One on screen at a time.

plates.description: One pre-rendered plate per aspect. The aspects share one clock and agree on length to within two frames. A format is built only if every beat has a plate for it.

plate.description: Exactly one of file and sequence. The aspect of width over height must be 16:9 for landscape, 9:16 for portrait and 1:1 for square, to within one percent.

file.description: An H.264 yuv420p .mp4 at the film's frame rate. Mastering containers are refused by name.

sequence.description: A frame sequence the kit encodes to H.264 at import (CRF 14, BT.709, one thread, bit-exact).

pattern.description: A printf-style path with a counter: frames/landscape/sally/%05d.png.

sha256.description: Of the file's bytes; for a sequence, of the frames' bytes concatenated in order.

subject.description: What the plate is about, as fractions of this aspect's frame. The kit's caption, subtitles and label may cover at most 2 percent of it.

camera.description: How the camera moved. Recorded for audit, never interpreted.

label.description: Printed for as long as the picture is up, verbatim: 'Real screenshot of <Name> from a Companion Hub QA run. Not a recording of this family.' An insert with no label is refused.

engine.description: The local, seeded model. No cloud text-to-speech.

atS.description: Seconds into the beat the recording starts. It may not run past the end of the plate.

text.description: The exact words the recording reads.
